title: Comprehensive Respiratory Set 1: Integrative Physiology (Short Answer)

questions.prompt: What is the typical status of the A-a gradient in a person suffering from hypoxemia strictly due to high altitude?
questions.modelAnswer: The A-a gradient remains normal (<10 mmHg).

questions.prompt: Which renal enzyme is inhibited by acetazolamide, and how does the resulting change in bicarbonate excretion facilitate high-altitude acclimatization?
questions.modelAnswer: Carbonic anhydrase; it increases bicarbonate excretion, causing a mild metabolic acidosis that offsets respiratory alkalosis and stabilizes the drive to breathe.

questions.prompt: During moderate exercise, do the mean values of arterial P_(O2)and P_(CO2)  typically increase, decrease, or remain constant?
What is the clinical term for the increase in ventilation rate that specifically matches the increased VO2and VCO2  during exercise?
List the three primary factors that cause the O2 -haemoglobin dissociation curve to shift to the right during physical exertion.
questions.modelAnswer: Increased P_(CO2), decreased pH (increased H^+), and increased temperature.

questions.prompt: In a patient with emphysema, how is the slope of the pressure-volume curve altered compared to a healthy individual?
questions.modelAnswer: The slope is steeper, representing increased lung compliance.

questions.prompt: Define the FEV_1 /FVC ratio and state its approximate normal value in a healthy adult.
questions.modelAnswer: It is the fraction of the forced vital capacity expired in one second; normal value is approximately 0.8 (80%).

questions.prompt: How is the total lung capacity (TLC) typically affected in restrictive lung diseases such as pulmonary fibrosis?
Which specific lung volumes or capacities are increased in obstructive lung diseases due to the phenomenon of "air trapping"?
questions.modelAnswer: Residual Volume (RV), Functional Residual Capacity (FRC), and Total Lung Capacity (TLC).

questions.prompt: Describe the effect of chronic global alveolar hypoxia at high altitude on pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular morphology.
questions.modelAnswer: It causes increased pulmonary vascular resistance (pulmonary hypertension) and right ventricular hypertrophy.

questions.prompt: Which specific classification of hypoxia is characterized by a normal Pa_(O2)and normal O2delivery but an abnormally high P_(O2)  in mixed venous blood?
Distinguish between "pink puffers" and "blue bloaters" regarding their arterial P_(CO2)  levels and the presence of secondary heart failure.
questions.modelAnswer: Pink puffers (primarily emphysema) have relatively normal P_(CO2); blue bloaters (primarily bronchitis) have hypercapnia and right ventricular failure (edema).

questions.prompt: Why does the administration of 100% O2have a limited effect on raising Pa_(O2)  in a patient with a significant right-to-left cardiac shunt?
questions.modelAnswer: Because the shunted blood never contacts ventilated alveoli, continuing to dilute the oxygenated blood regardless of inspired P_(O2).

questions.prompt: Identify the specific stimulus for the renal synthesis of erythropoietin during the process of high-altitude adaptation.
questions.modelAnswer: Renal hypoxia (decreased oxygen delivery to the kidneys).

questions.prompt: What happens to the distribution of ventilation/perfusion (V˙/Q˙ ) ratios throughout the lung during strenuous exercise?
questions.modelAnswer: The distribution ofV˙/Q˙ratios becomes more uniform or even.
